summary: Eleven code-mismatch findings across register (HTTP 201 vs 200, wrong error code DUPLICATE_EMAIL vs EMAIL_ALREADY_REGISTERED, name max=80 vs max=120), login (missing user sub-object in response), refresh (tokenType claim not validated — ACCESS token accepted as REFRESH), profile.read (method GET + path /me vs POST /read, error code USER_NOT_FOUND vs NOT_FOUND, missing 4 required response fields), and tokenType claim values lowercase vs uppercase. Logout, profile.update, address.create/list/update/delete are 501 stubs — accepted per scope. address.set-default is fully implemented and conforms.

findings.description: Register returns HTTP 201 Created. Spec (identity-auth/register.md, td.json response_schema) requires HTTP 200 OK.
findings.recommendation: Change `http.StatusCreated` to `http.StatusOK` in the Register handler success response.

findings.description: Duplicate-email error code is EMAIL_ALREADY_REGISTERED. Spec (td.json error_contract, identity-auth/register.md) requires code DUPLICATE_EMAIL.
findings.recommendation: Change the error code string to "DUPLICATE_EMAIL" to match the TD spec. Also align ErrEmailAlreadyRegistered sentinel if used downstream.

findings.description: Register request struct enforces name max=80 chars. TD spec and identity-auth/register.md require maxLength: 120.
findings.recommendation: Change the binding tag to `max=120` for the Name field in registerRequest.

findings.description: Login response struct returns flat fields (accessToken, refreshToken, accessTokenExpiresAt, refreshTokenExpiresAt, role). The spec (td.json, identity-auth/login.md) requires a nested user object: data.user.{userId, email, name, role}. email and name are entirely absent from the response.
findings.recommendation: Restructure loginResponse to include a User sub-object with userId, email, name, role. Update service.Login() signature or pass user data back from the service.

findings.description: The Refresh service calls parser.ValidateClaims which checks exp/iat/iss/aud but does NOT check that tokenType == "REFRESH" (or "refresh"). An ACCESS token can therefore be accepted as a refresh token. TD spec validation_rules explicitly require: "JWT tokenType claim must be REFRESH".
findings.recommendation: After ParseToken succeeds, extract claims.Extra["tokenType"] and verify it equals the expected REFRESH value. Return ErrAuthInvalid if the check fails.

findings.description: Profile read is registered as GET /api/v1/identity/profile/me. TD spec and identity-profile/read.md define method POST at path /api/v1/identity/profile/read. Both method and path differ from spec.
findings.recommendation: Change the route to profile.POST("/read", h.ProfileRead) to match the TD contract.

findings.description: Profile read returns error code USER_NOT_FOUND when the user is not found. TD spec and identity-profile/read.md require code NOT_FOUND (HTTP 404).
findings.recommendation: Change the not-found error code string to "NOT_FOUND".

findings.description: Profile read response struct contains only {userId, email, name, phone, role}. TD spec and identity-profile/read.md require 8 fields: userId, email, name, phone, defaultAddressId, role, status, createdAt, updatedAt. Missing: defaultAddressId, status, createdAt, updatedAt. Additionally the storage query in storage_user.go GetByID does not join addresses for defaultAddressId.
findings.recommendation: Extend profileReadResponse to include all 8 required fields. Update the storage query to LEFT JOIN addresses for defaultAddressId, and map all fields from the User domain object.

findings.description: tokenType claim values are lowercase "access" and "refresh". TD spec and identity-auth specs require uppercase "ACCESS" and "REFRESH" (per cross-cutting.auth claims spec: tokenType=ACCESS / tokenType=REFRESH). This affects both signing and the (missing) validation in Refresh.
findings.recommendation: Change constants to tokenTypeAccess = "ACCESS" and tokenTypeRefresh = "REFRESH".

findings.description: Tests assert success code is "0000" but the spec envelope uses code "SUCCESS" (wrapper.CodeSuccess). If wrapper.CodeSuccess is indeed "0000" this is an internal naming issue; if wrapper.CodeSuccess is "SUCCESS" the tests misrepresent the expected value. This must be verified against common/wrapper constants.
findings.recommendation: Verify wrapper.CodeSuccess value. If it is "SUCCESS", update test assertions. If it is "0000", verify that the spec accepts "0000" as the SUCCESS code.

findings.locus: app/identity/handler_login_test.go (handler_login_test.go) — no test for user sub-object fields email/name
findings.description: Login tests do not assert presence of email or name in the response user sub-object (those fields are missing from the response struct entirely per QA-IDENT-004). Once IDENT-004 is fixed, tests must be extended to assert data.user.email and data.user.name.
findings.recommendation: After fixing IDENT-004, extend login test assertions to cover data.user.{userId, email, name, role}.
